# Control Details Summary

## Process
- Process ID: PRC-IAM-014
- Process name: User Account Password Reset (Service Desk Assisted)
- Business line: Group Technology — Identity & Access Management Operations
- Risk domain: Information & Cyber Security (ICS)
- Process owner: Head of IAM Operations
- Document reference and version: CD-PRC-IAM-014 v3.2 (control inventory ref. CI-2026-IAM-014)
- Effective from: 01 January 2026

## Scope
- In scope:
  - Standard (non-privileged) employee, contractor and third-party accounts in ADX.
  - Password resets requested through the IT Service Desk (telephone or ServiceNow ticket).
  - Resets performed by Service Desk agents in the Bratislava and Amsterdam hubs.
- Out of scope:
  - Self-service password reset via the colleague portal (PRC-IAM-015).
  - Privileged and administrative accounts, Tier 0 / Tier 1 (PRC-IAM-021).
  - Customer-facing retail and wholesale banking credentials (PRC-CHN-004).
  - Local application passwords not federated to ADX.

## Risks
| Risk ID | Risk description (one sentence) | Covered by control |
|---|---|---|
| R-ICS-0071 | An unauthorised party obtains account access by fraudulently requesting a password reset. | CTL-IAM-0472 |
| R-ICS-0088 | Temporary credentials stay valid too long, are reused, or are sent over an insecure channel. | CTL-IAM-0473 |
| R-ICS-0103 | Reset activity is not completely logged or reviewed, so unauthorised resets go undetected. | CTL-IAM-0474 |

## Controls

### CTL-IAM-0472 — Caller identity verification prior to password reset
- Key control: Yes
- Control type: Preventive
- Control nature: Manual (IT-dependent)
- Frequency: Event-driven — every password reset request
- Control performer: IT Service Desk Agent (Level 1)
- Control reviewer: NOT STATED
- Control owner: Head of IT Service Desk Operations
- Systems involved: ServiceNow (ticket type "SD"), Verify-ID colleague lookup, Mobile Authenticator, ADX directory
- Policy reference: GISP-4.2.3; STD-IAM-07 §5.1
- What must happen:
  - Verify identity using at least two of three approved factors before any reset.
  - Factor A: one-time code pushed to the registered Mobile Authenticator and read back correctly.
  - Factor B: caller correctly answers employee number, cost centre code and line manager name from Verify-ID; public directory attributes may not be used.
  - Factor C: video call showing a valid corporate ID badge matching the Verify-ID photograph.
  - Record factors and outcome in the ticket's "Identity Verification" section before the reset is executed.
  - On failed or refused verification: no reset, close as "Rejected — identity not verified", raise a SEC ticket within one hour of the attempt.
- Expected evidence:
  - ServiceNow ticket export (PDF or Excel) with completed Identity Verification section, ticket number, timestamps and acting agent.
  - Mobile Authenticator push challenge log extract (Excel) where Factor A was used.
  - SEC incident ticket export for any rejected request.

### CTL-IAM-0473 — Temporary password issuance and forced change at first logon
- Key control: Yes
- Control type: Preventive
- Control nature: Automated (manually initiated)
- Frequency: Event-driven — every password reset executed
- Control performer: ADX Password Service (automated); initiated by IT Service Desk Agent
- Control reviewer: NOT STATED
- Control owner: Head of IAM Operations
- Systems involved: ADX Password Reset Tool v4.1, ADX directory, corporate SMS gateway
- Policy reference: STD-IAM-07 §5.4; BL-SEC-012
- What must happen:
  - Temporary password generated by the tool; never chosen, viewed or composed by the agent; parameters cannot be overridden.
  - Minimum 12 characters, meeting BL-SEC-012 complexity.
  - Single use; invalidated after first successful authentication.
  - Maximum validity 60 minutes from generation.
  - "User must change password at next logon" flag set automatically.
  - Delivered only by SMS to the registered mobile number, or by secure link to the line manager where none is registered.
  - No verbal, e-mail, chat or other delivery.
  - Generation, delivery and first use written to the ADX audit log.
- Expected evidence:
  - ADX Password Reset Tool configuration export (PDF screenshot or settings export) for the testing period.
  - ADX audit log extract (Excel) with generation, expiry, forced-change flag and first-use timestamps per reset.
  - SMS gateway delivery log extract (Excel) with masked destination and delivery status.

### CTL-IAM-0474 — Monthly reconciliation of password reset activity to approved tickets
- Key control: Yes
- Control type: Detective
- Control nature: Manual
- Frequency: Monthly — completed by the 10th working day following month end
- Control performer: IAM Operations Analyst
- Control reviewer: IAM Operations Manager (independent of the performer)
- Control owner: Head of IAM Operations
- Systems involved: ADX audit log, ServiceNow, IAM Exception Register (SharePoint list)
- Policy reference: STD-IAM-07 §7.2; Non-Financial Risk Framework §3.4
- What must happen:
  - Within 10 working days of month end, extract all reset events for the preceding month and reconcile each to an approved ticket with a completed Identity Verification section.
  - Record as exception: no matching ticket, ticket lacking completed verification, or acting agent differing from the ticket's agent.
  - Investigate and close each exception within five working days.
  - Confirmed unauthorised reset: escalate to the CISO office and raise a SEC incident the same working day.
  - Reconciliation reviewed and approved by the IAM Operations Manager by dated e-mail or electronic sign-off; no self-approval.
- Expected evidence:
  - Monthly reconciliation workbook (Excel) with matched population, unmatched items and sign-off tab.
  - ADX audit log extract (Excel or CSV) used as the source population.
  - IAM Exception Register extract (Excel) with exceptions, investigation notes and closure dates.
  - Reviewer approval e-mail (.msg) showing sender, recipients, date and approval wording.

## Rating definitions
| Rating | Definition (condensed to one sentence) |
|---|---|
| Effective | Operated as described all period, with no exceptions or only isolated, immaterial ones. |
| Partially effective | Operated for most of the period, but exceptions show a weakness needing remediation within appetite. |
| Ineffective | Did not operate as described, or exceptions mean it cannot be relied upon. |
| Inconclusive | Evidence insufficient, incomplete or inconsistent; refer to the control owner before rating. |
